## 2026-05-16 - V5 UI Stage 10: Hierarchy Brightening, Text-Block Surface, Button Active States

Applied the design reference hierarchy rule (primary content at maximum brightness), gave log/output areas a distinct terminal surface, and completed the button active-state set. CSS-only — no HTML, JS, or attribute changes.

Changes:

- `styles.css` `.brand-name`: Added `color: var(--grey-50)` — the app name is the top-level identity element; it receives maximum brightness
- `styles.css` `.metric strong`: Added `color: var(--grey-50)` — the large number is the primary data point in a metric card; it receives maximum brightness
- `styles.css` `.panel-heading h2, .panel-heading h3`: Added `color: var(--grey-50)` — panel headings are the primary label on a panel surface; body text inherits `--grey-100` from body, headings stand one step brighter
- `styles.css` `.text-block`: Added `padding: var(--space-4) var(--space-5)`, `background: var(--grey-900)`, `border: 1px solid var(--grey-700)`, `border-radius: 2px` — log and output areas now render as a distinct recessed terminal surface (one shade darker than the `--grey-800` panel background); the Stage 6 scrollbar styling applies automatically to the scrollable overflow
- `styles.css` `.nav-button:active`: `background: var(--grey-700)` — one step darker than the default `--grey-800` surface
- `styles.css` `.secondary-button:active`: `background: var(--grey-700); border-color: var(--blue-400)` — confirms click with both background and border shift
- `styles.css` `.danger-button:active`: `background: var(--red-700); border-color: var(--red-500)` — deepens into the red palette on click; `.primary-button:active` was already defined (Stage 2); all four button classes now have active states

Validation:

```powershell
# Hierarchy colors present
Select-String -Path styles.css -Pattern "grey-50" | Where-Object { $_.Line -match "brand-name|metric strong|panel-heading" }
# Returns results for all three.

# Text-block surface present
Select-String -Path styles.css -Pattern "\.text-block" -A 8 | Where-Object { $_.Line -match "grey-900|grey-700" }
# Returns background and border lines.

# Active states present
Select-String -Path styles.css -Pattern ":active"
# Returns results for nav-button, secondary-button, danger-button, primary-button.
```

Regression risk: none. Hierarchy color additions only affect elements that previously inherited `--grey-100`; `--grey-50` is one step brighter. Text-block padding/background is additive — the block now has its own surface but the same text content. Active states are new pseudo-class rules that only fire during the click press moment.

## 2026-05-16 - V5 UI Stage 8: Button Focus-Visible, Input Hover, Selection Color, Reduced Motion

Four accessibility and polish additions to `styles.css`. No HTML, JS, or attribute changes.

Changes:

- `styles.css` `::selection`: `background: var(--blue-700)`; `color: var(--grey-50)` — text selection now uses the dark-mode blue palette instead of the OS default (bright light-blue on dark backgrounds)
- `styles.css` `input:hover, select:hover`: `border-color: var(--grey-400)` — a subtle pre-focus signal; `textarea` intentionally excluded (its resize handle already indicates interactivity)
- `styles.css` `.nav-button:focus-visible, .secondary-button:focus-visible, .danger-button:focus-visible, .primary-button:focus-visible`: `outline: none; box-shadow: var(--focus-ring)` — wires the same blue halo used on inputs to all keyboard-focusable buttons; previously the `--focus-ring` token was defined and used on inputs but buttons had no visible keyboard ring
- `styles.css` `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)`: collapses `transition-duration` and `animation-duration` to `0.01ms` with `!important` on all elements — respects the OS accessibility setting for users who experience motion discomfort; ensures the Stage 6 transitions do not fire for those users

Validation:

```powershell
# focus-visible on buttons present
Select-String -Path styles.css -Pattern "focus-visible"
# Returns results for button selectors and (existing) tr[data-selectable-row] rule.

# reduced-motion block present
Select-String -Path styles.css -Pattern "prefers-reduced-motion"
# Returns 1 result.

# selection rule present
Select-String -Path styles.css -Pattern "::selection"
# Returns 1 result.
```

Regression risk: none. All rules are additive. `prefers-reduced-motion` only activates when the user has enabled that OS setting. `::selection` only changes the color of selected text. `input:hover` does not override `input:focus` (focus takes precedence in cascade). Focus-visible rules use the already-established `--focus-ring` token.

## 2026-05-16 - V5 UI Stage 6: Scrollbar Styling, Transitions, Empty State Component

Three polish additions to `styles.css`. No HTML, JS, or attribute changes.

Changes:

- `styles.css` `::-webkit-scrollbar*`: Custom thin (6px) scrollbar — grey-900 track, grey-600 thumb, grey-500 thumb on hover, rounded corners; replaces the default wide Windows light-mode scrollbar that was visually inconsistent with the dark app shell; applies to all scrollable areas including table wrappers and the sidebar
- `styles.css` `button { transition }`: Added `transition: background 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease, color 150ms ease` — all buttons (nav, secondary, danger, primary) now interpolate hover and focus changes smoothly; the base transition rule is inheritable so any future button variant picks it up automatically
- `styles.css` `input, select, textarea { transition }`: Added `transition: border-color 150ms ease, box-shadow 150ms ease` — focus ring and error border appear smoothly rather than snapping
- `styles.css` `.empty-state`, `.empty-state-label`, `.empty-state-hint`: New component for zero-data states; centered flex column, 120px minimum height, grey-400/500 muted text; two child elements for a bolded label and a smaller hint line; to be placed by Codex (Stage 7) inside panels and table wrappers that can be empty at runtime

Validation:

```powershell

# Returns at least 1 result.
```

Regression risk: low. Scrollbar is cosmetic-only (`::-webkit-scrollbar` does not affect layout). Transitions are additive and do not alter final states. Empty state class is unused until Stage 7 places the HTML elements.

## 2026-05-15 - WebView Hardening Review: UNC Normalization, Silent Snap, Gate And Smoke Fixes

### What changed

Worked through all 10 targets in `CLAUDE_REVIEW_TARGETS_RECENT_WEBVIEW_HARDENING.md`. Ran 76 tests (all pass before and after). Applied four patches:

1. **BUG: UNC path normalization (3 JS files)** `crossPageNormalizePath` / `completedProofNormalizePath` / `pendingCompletedCorrelationNormalizePath` used `.replace(/\+/g, '\')` which collapsed the leading `\` of UNC paths to `\`. Fixed by preserving the UNC prefix before the collapse. Applies to `crossPageContextView.js`, `completedView.js`, `pendingPublishView.js`.
2. **BUG: Silent sample-set snap to rows[0]** If the selected sample-set row disappeared after a refresh, `renderSampleValidationSampleSetGuide` silently promoted `rows[0]`, meaning a click of "Use Selected Category" could apply the wrong `category_key`. Fixed: non-empty disappeared key now clears with a visible message; `selectedSampleValidationSampleSet` no longer falls back to `rows[0]` when no key is set.
3. **TEST GAP: Completed/pending proof smoke no-mutation boundary** Upgraded from a blanket `posts.length !== 0` check to an explicit forbidden-route list (matching the sample-validation smoke pattern). Updated the scaffold assertion to expect the forbidden-list guard.
4. **TEST GAP: Tauri startup gate missing pendingPublishView.js** Added `pendingSampleValidationHandoffLines` and `pendingDrainGuardState` fragment checks to `validate_backend_web_ui` in `lib.rs`.

### Remaining wording risk (deferred)

`pendingPublishReadinessStatus()` returns `Ready to drain` at the page-level chip while detail rows use `Ready-looking`. Inconsistent phrasing; deferred as a cosmetic-only change requiring coordinated test updates.

Maintained the full Table of Contents in the `## Navigation` section of `REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`, grouped by date (newest first). The TOC replaces the previous "scroll past this table" stub text and covers all 10 date groups from 2026-05-06 to 2026-05-15.

- Added design-only repair/reconcile contracts to `/api/contract` for:

  - `completed.repair_sidecar_metadata`
  - `pending_publish.repair_manifest`

- Each contract publishes `mutation_enabled=false`, `frontend_allowed=false`, candidate command name, owner surface, mutation class, required preconditions, required evidence, rollback requirements, prohibited actions, and a safe next step.
- Added `repair_reconcile_summary` to the contract payload with `status=design_only_no_mutation_routes`.
- Updated WebView API Contract safety review to render a `Repair/reconcile boundary` row from backend contract data.
- Kept route count unchanged and added no repair/reconcile command routes or mutation controls.

- `Docs\V5_TRANSITION_STATUS_BOARD.md`
- `Docs\TLDR.md`

### Implementation

- Added `ScheduleStopWatcherManager`, a backend-owned daemon watcher that monitors the launched pipeline process and writes the normal `pipeline_stop.flag` when the active schedule window reaches its end.
- The watcher arms only for backend-started `continuous` pipeline runs where schedule enforcement is enabled, `Ignore Schedule` was not selected, and the schedule payload reports a current stop boundary.
- The watcher exits without writing a stop flag if the process finishes first, reports errors if process polling or flag writing fails, and is canceled when the local API server stops.
- Scheduled WebView `continuous` starts are now allowed when the backend watcher is available. `Ignore Schedule` remains a high-review bypass and does not arm the watcher.
- Launch backend preflight now reports watcher readiness instead of treating all scheduled continuous starts as blocked.
- Schedule and Launch WebView copy now explains that the Schedule page can edit schedule state but cannot start or directly arm the watcher; Launch backend preflight/start owns the watcher lifecycle.

### Validation

- `python -m unittest DesktopApp.tests.test_schedule_stop_watcher DesktopApp.tests.test_facade_process_schedule_policy -q`: passed.
- `python -m unittest DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade.ApplicationFacadeTests.test_pipeline_start_respects_schedule_gate_before_web_launch_ui DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade.ApplicationFacadeTests.test_pipeline_start_allows_scheduled_continuous_with_backend_watcher_available DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade.ApplicationFacadeTests.test_pipeline_start_blocked_by_active_work_does_not_cancel_existing_schedule_watcher DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade.ApplicationFacadeTests.test_launch_preflight_reports_continuous_schedule_stop_watcher_boundary DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade.ApplicationFacadeTests.test_launch_preflight_reports_schedule_and_lock_blocks_without_launching DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade.LocalApiServerTests.test_local_api_scheduled_continuous_start_arms_backend_stop_watcher -q`: passed.
- `python -m unittest DesktopApp.tests.test_webview_schedule_smoke -q`: passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium. This intentionally changes WebView/backend scheduled `continuous` start behavior from blocked to allowed when the backend can arm a stop-at-window-end watcher. It does not change Tk, PowerShell media processing, queue scope, FFmpeg routing, source/output/scratch behavior, or V4. Remaining risk is lifecycle: if the local API process itself is killed before the deadline, no in-process watcher can write a later stop flag.

### Implementation

- The reconciliation payload compares recent validation records against bounded current backend artifacts: Queue snapshot source evidence, Completed manifest source/output proof, Pending Publish manifest/path clues, and recent RunLogs text.
- Recent validation rows are labeled `current`, `review`, `stale`, or `unknown` with exact current-match booleans, missing-current-evidence notes, and safe next action text.

A package could pass backend contract checks while opening a blank or partially broken WebView if static assets drifted after the WebView module split.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\tauri_shell\src-tauri\src\lib.rs`
- `DesktopApp\tauri_shell\README.md`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_tauri_shell_scaffold.py`
- `Docs\V5_TAURI_TRANSITION_CURRENT_PLAN.md`
- `Docs\TAURI_WEBVIEW_PARITY_MATRIX.md`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added `validate_backend_web_ui()` to the Rust Tauri shell startup path after health and route-contract validation, before the WebView window is built.
- The gate fetches the backend-served `/`, `/assets/app.js`, and `/assets/crossPageContextView.js` through the same local backend request path and verifies critical fragments for bootstrap injection, Home/Settings/Diagnostics panels, the real-media validation worksheet, refresh coordination, settings handoff, and cross-page worksheet helpers.
- Added Rust failure-injection tests for valid assets and missing real-media worksheet fragments, including no-token-leak checks in error strings.
- Updated Tauri scaffold tests and README wording so the launch smoke is documented as backend + WebView asset validation, not only process/window lifecycle validation.

### Validation

- Added static Python coverage for the new Rust startup gate and Rust unit-test names.
- Ran Rust unit tests, focused Tauri scaffold/static tests, the full desktop suite, Tauri build checks, release self-test, and the live Tauri launch/close smoke listed in the session report.

### Regression Risk

Low to medium. This is a startup gate, so it can stop Tauri preview launch earlier if static assets are missing or stale. That is deliberate: it fails before opening a broken shell. It does not change Tk, V4, backend command contracts, media policy, filesystem mutation, or local API route behavior.

That slowed real-media validation and made it easier to miss stale runtime failures, missing outputs, sidecar mismatches, size growth, or pending-publish blockers.

### Implementation

- Added Queue selected-row review checklist text that summarizes row state, operator status, route decision, runtime history, deferred checks, review flags, blockers, runtime issues, and safe next action.
- Added Completed selected-row review checklist text that summarizes output health, consistency, sidecar state, size growth over policy, runtime conflicts, review flags, consistency issues, and safe next action.
- Added Pending Publish selected-row review checklist text that summarizes drain recommendation, diagnostic status/severity, health blockers, recommended open targets, issue summaries, and safe next action.
- Replaced generic unselected detail text with the same checklist structure so empty detail panes tell the operator exactly what selecting a row will provide.
- Kept every selected-row checklist read-only; launch, repair, reconcile, rerun, drain, delete, rewrite, and publish behavior remains backend-owned.

## 2026-05-13 - Queue Deferred Runtime Check Visibility

### Root Problem

- Path-order controls only change local text input and tell the operator to rerun backend Preview before applying.

- Tauri shell build checker passed WebView JavaScript syntax checks and Rust `cargo check`.
- Full desktop unittest discovery suite: 993 tests passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium-low. This exposes an existing backend multi-source contract in the WebView, but the mutation path remains backend-owned. Main risk is operator selection confusion, mitigated by checked-row count, confirmation text, disabled blocked rows, and fallback to single selected-row apply when nothing is checked.

## 2026-05-08 - Web API GET Timeout Guard

The WebView refresh coordinator coalesces overlapping refreshes, but the shared browser API client used unbounded `fetch()` calls. A single hung backend read could leave `refreshInFlight` true indefinitely, causing future manual and interval refreshes to queue behind a request that would never settle.

- Timeout failures now raise a clear `Request timed out after ... ms` error for existing page-level refresh/status handling.

### Validation

- Full desktop unittest discovery suite: 768 tests passed.
- Tauri shell build checker passed WebView JavaScript syntax checks and Rust `cargo check`.

Low to medium. GET refreshes can now fail visibly after 30 seconds instead of waiting forever. Long-running POST commands are intentionally unchanged unless a future caller opts into a timeout.

## 2026-05-08 - Coordinator Runtime Config Guardrails

## 2026-05-08 - Local API Request And Static Asset Guards

### Root Problem

The local API JSON body reader rejected oversized and non-numeric `Content-Length` values, but it did not reject negative lengths. Passing `-1` into a stream read can read until EOF or block depending on the stream, which is the wrong behavior for a local command API. Static asset resolution also relied on lexical path checks without verifying the final resolved path remained below the asset root.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\http_helpers.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_api_http_helpers.py`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`
- `Docs\V5_TAURI_TRANSITION_CURRENT_PLAN.md`

### Implementation

- Reject negative `Content-Length` values with the existing `invalid content length` 400 response before reading from the request body.
- Resolve static asset candidates against the asset root and reject any path whose final resolved location escapes that root.
- Added direct tests for negative lengths, oversized lengths, zero-length JSON-body defaults, and static asset traversal rejection.

### Validation

- Focused API HTTP helper tests: 4 tests passed.
- Full desktop unittest discovery suite: 739 tests passed.

### Regression Risk

Low. Valid requests and static asset URLs are unchanged; malformed negative-length requests now fail fast, and asset resolution now has an additional resolved-path containment check.

## 2026-05-08 - Runtime Artifact Diagnostics and Close Guard Hardening

### Root Problem

ActiveJobs reconciliation could silently skip malformed runtime records, close-readiness could fail open if related-process inspection itself crashed, and pending-publish preview did not flag duplicate manifests pointing to the same parked payload or destination. In long-running workstation use, these cases hide the exact artifacts/operators need to inspect before deciding whether it is safe to close, restart, or drain pending publishes.

### Implementation

- ActiveJobs reconciliation now returns and logs a warning when the folder cannot be reconciled or a record is malformed.
- ActiveJobs process-completion updates now log when a corrupt record is repaired with default fields.
- Close-readiness now fails closed when related MediaPipeline process inspection, fresh pipeline progress, or fresh audit progress cannot be verified, reporting the verification error instead of treating the shell as safe to close.

- Control flag reads now log unreadable pause/stop/rescan flag files instead of silently falling back to filesystem mtime.
- Expanded the web Diagnostics page to expose existing backend-allowlisted Open buttons for config file, ActiveJobs, queue snapshot, completed manifest, last stdout/stderr logs, and failure markers.

Low to medium. The only behavior change is stricter close-readiness when process/progress inspection fails. That may block closing in ambiguous states, but it is the safer default for unattended media processing.

## 2026-05-08 - ActiveJobs Close-Readiness Guard

### Root Problem

The Tauri/WebView2 transition plan identified process lifecycle and shell close behavior as the next highest-value hardening area. Close readiness already checked related running processes plus fresh pipeline/audit progress, but it did not directly treat non-terminal `ActiveJobs` records as a close blocker. That left a gap where the shell could report safe-to-close if the snapshot looked idle while `ActiveJobs` still contained a live, launching, or unverifiable process record.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_process_active_jobs.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_process_active_job_runner.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_processes.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\application\facade_process_guard.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\command_payloads_policy.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\command_payloads_process.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_service_process_active_jobs.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_api_command_payloads_policy.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_application_facade.py`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added `active_job_close_block_messages()` to scan recent `ActiveJobs` records for `launching` or `active` jobs.
- Treats live PIDs, missing PIDs, unverifiable PIDs, unreadable records, and malformed records as close-readiness blockers.
- Does not block on records whose PID is definitely gone, allowing normal reconciliation to mark those orphaned.
- Added a `ProcessLifecycleServiceMixin.active_job_close_block_messages()` compatibility wrapper.
- Updated close-readiness guard behavior so `Shell close` is blocked when `ActiveJobs` still reports active work, even if the current snapshot appears idle.
- Updated the backend shutdown command payload so direct shutdown requests still set the shutdown event but return `severity="warning"` and include close-readiness data when active work is detected.
- Deferred the backend shutdown callback briefly until after the JSON command response is built, reducing the chance that the standalone backend stops before the Tauri shell receives the shutdown response.
- Added a Local API lifecycle test for an idle snapshot with a `launching` ActiveJobs record, covering both close-readiness and authenticated backend-shutdown warning behavior.

### Validation

- Focused ActiveJobs, service-wrapper, API payload, Local API lifecycle, and close-readiness tests: 13 tests passed.
- Python AST syntax checks for touched lifecycle/API test modules: passed.
- Full desktop unittest discovery suite: 680 tests passed.
- Note: direct `py_compile` on `test_application_facade.py` hit a transient Windows `__pycache__` access-denied replace error after focused tests; AST parsing and full unittest discovery both passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium-low. This intentionally makes shell close-readiness more conservative when `ActiveJobs` cannot be verified. A stale malformed active-job record may now cause the shell to warn instead of reporting safe-to-close, but that is safer than silently closing while tracked process state is ambiguous. Existing forced-close behavior remains available through the shell confirmation path.

## 2026-05-08 - VLC Long-Path Junction Timeout Guard

## 2026-05-07 - ASS Subtitle Encoding Fallback Stabilization

### Root Problem

The bundled tool-integration check intermittently failed while converting a tiny ASS subtitle stream. The converter stopped at the first fallback encoding that `pysubs2` could parse; broad encodings such as `cp1252` can parse structurally damaged or mismatched bytes and still produce no usable dialogue text, causing a false "all events were filtered" failure.

### Files Changed

- `Pipeline\ass_to_srt_chatgpt.py`
- `Test-MediaPipelineRemuxEncodeAIO-Release.ps1`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added encoding-candidate diagnostics for ASS loads.
- Replaced first-success fallback selection with best-candidate selection based on usable dialogue text count, dialogue count, text length, replacement characters, and existing encoding order as the tie-breaker.
- Kept the existing encoding order, style filtering, karaoke filtering, and SRT rendering behavior otherwise unchanged.
- Added the ASS helper to release self-test layout and Python syntax checks.

### Validation

- Python syntax check for `Pipeline\ass_to_srt_chatgpt.py`: passed.
- Bundled tool-integration check repeated 5 times: passed.
- Full desktop unittest discovery suite: 198 tests passed.
- Release self-test: passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium-low. This touches subtitle conversion fallback behavior, but only after the preferred UTF-8 paths fail. The change is designed to avoid choosing a structurally parseable but text-empty fallback.

## 2026-05-07 - Tauri Backend Bootstrap Stdout Tolerance

### Root Problem

The Tauri shell expected the Python local API bootstrap JSON to be the first stdout line. That is normally true, but it made startup brittle if Python, a bundled dependency, or a future startup hook wrote a harmless warning before the bootstrap payload.

- `Docs\archive\historical-reviews\TAURI_WEBVIEW2_TRANSITION_GROUNDWORK.md`

### Implementation

- Replaced one-line bootstrap reading with a bounded bootstrap scanner.
- The shell now skips and logs non-JSON stdout before bootstrap until it sees a valid `desktop_local_api_bootstrap.v1` payload or the startup timeout expires.
- If JSON parses as a bootstrap payload but has the wrong schema, startup still fails deterministically.
- After bootstrap, stdout/stderr pipes continue draining so the backend cannot block on a full pipe.

## 2026-05-07 - Native Tauri Close Guard

### Root Problem

The web prototype could warn through `beforeunload`, and the backend exposed close readiness, but the Tauri shell itself still treated window close as an unconditional backend shutdown path. A native shell needs to consult backend-owned active-work state before closing so the operator cannot bypass the web warning by closing the desktop window.

- `DesktopApp\tauri_shell\src-tauri\Cargo.toml`

### Implementation

- Added a native close guard in the Tauri `WindowEvent::CloseRequested` handler.
- The shell now calls `GET /api/backend/close-readiness` with the per-run bearer token before shutdown.
- If the backend reports `safe_to_close=true`, close continues normally and the existing graceful backend shutdown path runs.
- If the backend reports active work, the shell shows a Windows-native confirmation dialog before allowing close.
- If close readiness cannot be verified, the shell also prompts before closing instead of silently shutting down.
- The existing `WindowEvent::Destroyed`, app-level exit cleanup, and `Drop` fallback remain intact.

## 2026-05-07 - Web Prototype Guarded CSV Rerun Launch

### Root Problem

CSV rerun is the highest-risk launch command in the current local API because it stages media files and parks rerun outputs. The backend had already narrowed the API to the conservative policy of copy staging, keep originals, and park returns. The web prototype needed to expose that command only in that constrained form, with no delete/move/replace options.

### Implementation

- Added a CSV Rerun section to the web Launch page.
- Requires a CSV path before sending a backend command.
- Hardcodes the safe policy payload: `stage_mode=copy`, `original_mode=keep`, `return_mode=park`, `dry_run=false`.
- Shows the policy in read-only form fields and requires browser confirmation before `POST /api/rerun/start`.
- Routes rerun start results into the existing Command Results history and rerun launch detail block.
- Kept unsafe move/delete/replace policies out of the web UI.

## 2026-05-07 - Web Prototype Guarded Pipeline Launch

### Root Problem

The local API already exposed `POST /api/pipeline/start`, but the web prototype intentionally kept launch commands hidden until the command-result pattern, schedule visibility, and operator confirmations were in place. A deeper inspection found a safety mismatch: the Tk controller owns schedule override prompts and stop-at-window-end bookkeeping, while the local API start path did not. Exposing launch buttons before correcting that would let the future web shell bypass schedule enforcement.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\application\facade.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\index.html`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\assets\app.js`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\assets\styles.css`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_application_facade.py`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`
- `Docs\archive\historical-reviews\TAURI_WEBVIEW2_TRANSITION_GROUNDWORK.md`

### Implementation

- Added a backend schedule gate to `MediaPipelineApplicationFacade.start_pipeline_process()`.
- Kept `validate` and `drain_pending_pushes` unscheduled, matching current intent.
- Allowed normal starts when schedule enforcement is off.
- Rejected outside-window starts unless the request explicitly carries `schedule_override=run_once` or `schedule_override=ignore`.
- Blocked scheduled `continuous` starts unless `schedule_override=ignore` is explicit, because the local API does not yet own the Tk schedule-stop watcher that writes Stop After Current at the end of a schedule window.
- Added a Launch page to the static web prototype with mode, sleep seconds, schedule override, show-config/show-console toggles, and a browser confirmation before `POST /api/pipeline/start`.
- Routed launch results into the existing Command Results history and launch detail block.
- Added regression coverage for schedule-gated pipeline starts and the Launch page wiring.

- Ran `python -m unittest DesktopApp.tests.test_application_facade`: 20 tests passed.

- Ran `python -m unittest discover -s DesktopApp\tests -p "test_*.py"` with bytecode disabled: 178 tests passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium. This intentionally tightens local API process-start behavior when schedule enforcement is enabled, which is safer for the future web shell but could block a previously possible API-only continuous launch. The Tk app path is unchanged and remains the production launcher.

## Current Remediation Status

The targeted remediation phases in this changelog are complete through Phase 11. All current phase entries have validation results recorded, and there are no remaining `Pending for this phase` markers.

Historical deferred notes in earlier entries are retained for audit traceability. Several of those deferrals were later resolved by follow-up phases:

- Native process callback consolidation was addressed by the Phase 2 follow-up.
- Pending publish transaction decomposition was addressed by Phases 3 and 4.
- Pending manifest state/schema drift was addressed by Phase 5.
- Event/progress, ActiveJobs, and control-flag contract drift were addressed by Phases 6 through 9.
- Stale pipeline and audit progress launch cleanup were addressed by Phases 10 and 11.

Longer-term architectural cleanup still remains outside this completed targeted pass: desktop app state-container extraction and broader PowerShell job-context decomposition should stay as future refactor work because they require larger compatibility shims and higher UI/pipeline regression risk.

## 2026-05-07 - Phase 11: Stale Audit Progress Launch Cleanup

### Root Problem

Audit runs had the same stale-progress visibility problem as pipeline runs: a previous `audit_progress.json` could remain visible after a stopped, killed, or crashed audit until the next audit wrote fresh state. This made the UI look like old audit work was still current during the new launch window.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_constants.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_processes.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\controllers\process_lifecycle_controller.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_process_service.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_controllers.py`
- `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`

### Implementation

- Added `AUDIT_PROGRESS_LAUNCH_CLEANUP_STALE_SECONDS` as a launch-specific stale threshold.
- Added `prepare_audit_runtime_for_launch()` to clear stale previous-run `audit_progress.json` only after launch overlap guards have passed.
- Added `_clear_audit_progress_artifacts()` so audit launch prep deletes only audit progress files and does not touch pipeline progress, pause/stop/rescan flags, or other runtime state.
- Added related-process protection: if a MediaPipeline process is still discoverable, stale audit progress is reported but left in place.
- Integrated audit runtime launch prep into `start_audit()`.
- Added tests for stale audit progress removal, pipeline progress preservation, related-process skip behavior, and controller launch-prep action logging.
- Added regression assertions to keep audit launch cleanup scoped and guarded.

### Validation

- Parsed the changed PowerShell regression script: passed.
- Ran targeted Python process/controller tests: 92 tests passed.
- Ran `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`: passed.
- Ran `python -m unittest discover -s DesktopApp\tests -p "test_*.py"` with bytecode disabled: 147 tests passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium. This deletes audit runtime progress files during audit launch preparation, but only when progress is stale beyond the launch threshold and no related process is detected. It does not delete media files, pipeline progress, queue files, control flags, manifests, or pending-publish artifacts.

## 2026-05-06 - Phase 2 Follow-Up: Callback-Capable Native Process Runner

### Root Problem

The original Phase 2 remediation added shared native-process contracts and safer timeout defaults, but intentionally left `Invoke-NativeCommand` and `Invoke-FFmpegWithProgress` on separate process loops. That meant FFmpeg still owned its own `ProcessStartInfo`, stderr read loop, stop polling, timeout handling, and kill/drain behavior while other tools used the generic native wrapper.

### Files Changed

- `Pipeline\Modules\Native.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\FfmpegProgress.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`

### Implementation

- Added `Invoke-NativeProcess`, a shared callback-capable runner for native tools.
- Moved process start, argument-array launch, stdout/stderr line draining, timeout kill, stop-flag polling, bounded drain, and result metadata into the shared runner.
- Kept `Invoke-NativeCommand` as the compatibility API, now backed by `Invoke-NativeProcess`.
- Rebuilt `Invoke-FFmpegWithProgress` as a progress-specific wrapper around `Invoke-NativeProcess` using a stderr-line callback for FFmpeg progress parsing.
- Preserved FFmpeg progress events, repro command behavior, stderr tailing, `LastFFmpeg*` compatibility variables, pause notification, timeout markers, and global process-handle cleanup.
- Made `Native.ps1` self-load `NativeProcessContracts.ps1` when standalone tooling dot-sources it outside the main pipeline module order.

### Validation

- Parsed changed PowerShell modules and reliability test script with `System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser`: passed.
- Ran `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`: passed.
- Ran `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ToolIntegrationChecks.ps1`: passed.
- Ran `python -m unittest discover -s DesktopApp\tests -p "test_*.py"`: 118 tests passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium. The public function names and return shape are preserved, but FFmpeg now relies on the shared process loop. The regression suite covers success, failure, timeout, start failure, repro command generation, progress updates, and bundled FFmpeg integration.

## 2026-05-06 - Phase 1: Subtitle Default-Language Policy

### Root Problem

The FFmpeg and mkvmerge subtitle builders hardcoded English (`eng`/`en`) as the default subtitle language. That conflicted with the configurable subtitle language policy and folder-level sidecar overrides, especially for operators who choose a non-English preferred subtitle language.

### Files Changed

- `Pipeline\Modules\Subtitles.Common.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\Subtitles.Builders.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`

### Implementation

- Added shared subtitle-default helpers that derive preferred defaults from `Get-SubtitleLanguagePolicy`.
- Kept undefined and blank language tracks as fallback-only candidates, so they do not steal default disposition ahead of a configured real language.
- Routed both mkvmerge and FFmpeg subtitle default selection through the shared helper.
- Preserved existing behavior where supplemental/signs tracks do not become default unless no better candidate exists.

### Validation

- Added regression coverage proving configured preferred language beats earlier undefined and English tracks in both FFmpeg and mkvmerge builders.
- Preserved existing undefined-before-English regression coverage.
- Ran `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1` with bundled PowerShell 7.6.0: passed.

### Regression Risk

Medium-low. Existing English defaults remain unchanged when `SubKeepLanguages` contains `eng`/`en`. Behavior changes only when the configured preferred subtitle language is non-English or folder policy overrides subtitle language lists.

## 2026-05-06 - Phase 2: Version Contracts, Pending Publish Health, and Safer Runtime Defaults

### Root Problem

Several audit findings were related rather than isolated: the app displayed a product version that did not match V4, persisted records only carried the sidecar compatibility version, pending-publish payload loss could be invisible outside logs, native tool timeout defaults were scattered and sometimes unbounded, CSV rerun arguments exposed unsafe modes that were later ignored, and config backup files were written next to the live PSD1. These issues made the system harder to diagnose and easier to misread during unattended Windows operation.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\__init__.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_config.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\service_pending_publish.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_pending_publish_service.py`
- `Pipeline\Audit-MediaLibrary_chatgpt.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Invoke-RerunCsv.ps1`
- `Pipeline\MediaPipeline_chatgpt.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\FfmpegProgress.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\Logging.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\Native.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\PendingPush.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\Sidecar.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\Versioning.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Schemas\media_pipeline_completed_job.schema.json`
- `Pipeline\Schemas\media_pipeline_pending_push_manifest.schema.json`
- `Pipeline\Schemas\media_pipeline_pipeline_event.schema.json`
- `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`

### Implementation

- Added `Pipeline\Modules\Versioning.ps1` so product version, sidecar schema version, and audit schema version are explicit contracts instead of a single overloaded value.
- Set the desktop product version to `v4.000` while preserving sidecar compatibility version `1.0`.
- Added `product_version` to sidecars, pending-publish manifests, pipeline events, and related JSON schemas without changing existing `pipeline_version` compatibility semantics.
- Updated pipeline and audit startup logging so operators can see both product version and schema/compatibility version.
- Added pending-publish health accounting for missing payloads and unreadable manifests in the PowerShell pending index.
- Surfaced pending-publish health rows in the desktop pending-publish service so missing parked payloads are visible to the UI instead of being hidden as only log noise.
- Centralized default native-tool timeouts with named defaults for `ffprobe`, `ffmpeg`, `mkvmerge`, Python helpers, and BDPGS OCR.
- Routed FFmpeg, FFmpeg progress, mkvmerge, and Python tool wrappers through those named defaults.
- Simplified CSV rerun CLI options to expose only the actually supported safe policies: copy-only staging, keep originals, and park outputs.
- Moved future desktop config backup files into `ConfigBackups` beside the active config file instead of mixing timestamped backups into the live config directory.

### Validation

- Parsed all changed PowerShell scripts with `System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser`: passed.
- Ran `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1` with bundled PowerShell 7.6.0: passed.
- Ran `python -m unittest discover -s DesktopApp\tests -p "test_*.py"`: 111 tests passed.
- Ran Python compile checks for changed desktop modules and tests: passed.
- Smoke-tested Python version exports: `APP_VERSION = v4.000`, `PIPELINE_SIDECAR_VERSION = 1.0`.
- Smoke-tested PowerShell version contract export: `ProductVersion = v4.000`, `PipelineSidecarVersion = 1.0`, `AuditSchemaVersion = 1.0`.

### Regression Risk

Medium. The product-version split is intentionally compatibility-preserving, but any external automation that assumed `pipeline_version` was the user-facing app version should now read `product_version`. Native tool wrappers now have finite default timeouts; the FFmpeg default is deliberately long, but extremely long encodes may need an explicit override if they exceed it.

### Intentionally Deferred

- Full process-runner consolidation remains deferred because merging all subprocess call paths at once would be behavior-changing around FFmpeg progress, native stderr capture, and cancellation.
- Full pending-publish transaction decomposition remains deferred because drain/retry semantics are production-sensitive and should be extracted behind compatibility wrappers.
- Desktop app state-container extraction remains deferred because the current `app.py` controller still owns many UI bindings; splitting it safely requires smaller controller-by-controller migrations.
- Pipeline job context and stage decomposition remain deferred because PowerShell ambient state is widespread and should be reduced by staged adapter extraction rather than a broad rewrite.

## 2026-05-06 - Phase 3: Pending Publish Module Split and Native Process Contracts

### Root Problem

The audit identified two related maintainability risks that could not be fixed safely with a rewrite-sized change: `PendingPush.ps1` was acting as a dense manifest store, health index, duplicate-detection index, crash-repair helper, park transaction, and drain transaction all at once; and native process execution shared behavior by convention rather than by an explicit result/timeout contract. Both areas were production-sensitive, so this pass split stable helper ownership without changing live publish/drain or FFmpeg progress semantics.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\contracts\completed_job.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\contracts\pending_publish.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\contracts\pipeline_events.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_contracts.py`
- `Pipeline\MediaPipeline_chatgpt.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\Native.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\NativeProcessContracts.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\PendingManifestStore.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\PendingPublishIndex.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Modules\PendingPush.ps1`
- `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`

### Implementation

- Extracted pending manifest accessors, manifest read/write, round-trip validation, retry-state persistence, and tx3g sidecar failure persistence into `Pipeline\Modules\PendingManifestStore.ps1`.
- Extracted pending publish index construction, health-row collection, refresh/reconciliation, and already-parked duplicate detection into `Pipeline\Modules\PendingPublishIndex.ps1`.
- Kept `Invoke-ParkPendingPush`, `Repair-PendingManifestState`, sidecar publish, and `Invoke-RetryPendingPushes` in `Pipeline\Modules\PendingPush.ps1` so park/drain behavior stayed stable.
- Routed raw manifest reads in pending park/index/drain paths through `Read-PendingManifestFile`.
- Added structural regression checks proving manifest persistence no longer lives in `PendingPush.ps1`, and pending index/health/match ownership lives in `PendingPublishIndex.ps1`.
- Added `Pipeline\Modules\NativeProcessContracts.ps1` for `New-NativeCommandResult`, native failure-code classification, external tool result metadata mutation, and named default timeout policy.
- Updated `Invoke-NativeCommand` to return `New-NativeCommandResult`, preserving the existing `ExitCode`, `Output`, `Error`, `Stdout`, `Stderr`, `TimedOut`, `Stopped`, and `ErrorCode` fields.
- Left `Invoke-NativeCommand` and `Invoke-FFmpegWithProgress` as separate runners for now; this pass only centralized shared contracts and timeout policy.
- Updated Python persisted-record contracts to parse optional `product_version` from pending-publish manifests, pipeline events, and completed sidecar/job records.

### Validation

- Parsed all changed PowerShell scripts with `System.Management.Automation.Language.Parser`: passed.
- Ran `Pipeline\Tests\Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1` with bundled PowerShell 7.6.0 after each extraction group: passed.
- Ran `python -m unittest discover -s DesktopApp\tests -p "test_*.py"`: 111 tests passed.
- Ran focused Python contract tests: 7 tests passed.
- Ran Python compile checks for changed contract modules and tests: passed.
- Ran release builder dry-run: passed; no files copied.

### Regression Risk

Medium-low. This was mostly extraction and contract surfacing. The highest-risk path touched was native result construction, but the returned field names and values were preserved and covered by the reliability harness. Pending publish behavior is intended to be unchanged; the park/drain transaction functions were deliberately left in place.

### Intentionally Deferred

- Full pending park/drain transaction-object extraction remains deferred. The next safe step is to isolate `Invoke-ParkPendingPush` into a `PendingParkTransaction` wrapper while keeping the current function as the public API.
- Full FFmpeg progress runner merge remains deferred. The progress runner reads stderr line-by-line for progress and bounded diagnostics, so merging it with the generic async-capture runner needs a callback-capable runner and dedicated timeout/stop tests.
- Desktop `app.py` state extraction remains deferred until controller ownership can be migrated in smaller UI-safe slices.
- PowerShell `PipelineJobContext` introduction remains deferred because the main remux/encode paths still rely on ambient `$script:*` state across many modules.

## 2026-05-07 - Tauri Shell App-Level Backend Cleanup

### Root Problem

The Tauri shell already requested Python backend shutdown during main-window close and destroy events, but the launch/close smoke exposed an intermittent orphaned backend when the shell process exited without the window hook being sufficient. A shell-owned backend must be cleaned up deterministically, otherwise each test or operator close can leave hidden localhost API processes running.

- `DesktopApp\tauri_shell\src-tauri\src\lib.rs`

### Implementation

- Changed the Tauri shell from shorthand `Builder::run()` to explicit `build()` plus `app.run(...)`.
- Added app-level cleanup for `RunEvent::ExitRequested` and `RunEvent::Exit`.
- Kept the existing `CloseRequested`, `Destroyed`, and `Drop` cleanup paths as independent fallbacks.
- Centralized backend-state shutdown lookup so every lifecycle path uses the same child-process cleanup behavior.

### Validation

- Ran `DesktopApp\tauri_shell\Test-TauriShell-Launch.ps1`: passed; the harness opened the dev shell, detected the actual Tauri process and backend PID, closed the shell, and verified backend cleanup.

### Regression Risk

Low. This adds another lifecycle cleanup path and preserves the existing graceful shutdown and force-kill fallback. The only behavior change is more deterministic backend termination when the Tauri shell exits.

## 2026-05-07 - Web Prototype Settings Patch Preview

### Root Problem

The web Settings page could show a redacted config snapshot and validate visible values, but exposing a direct save endpoint would be unsafe because sensitive values are intentionally rendered as `<redacted>`. Posting the visible table back as a full config could overwrite real secrets or token-like fields. The next safe migration step is a backend-owned patch preview that proves the future save contract without writing PSD1 files.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\application\facade.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\contract.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\server.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\index.html`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\assets\app.js`

- `Docs\archive\historical-reviews\TAURI_WEBVIEW2_TRANSITION_GROUNDWORK.md`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added token-protected `POST /api/settings/preview-patch` with `effect=none`.
- The endpoint accepts explicit `changes` and optional `remove_keys`, merges them with the backend's unredacted `resolved.config_data`, validates the merged result, and returns a `desktop_command_result.v1` envelope.
- Sensitive keys reject the literal `<redacted>` placeholder so the future save path cannot accidentally persist display placeholders.
- Returned diff data is redacted before it reaches the frontend; the command reports `writes_config=false`.
- Added a Settings page `Patch Preview` panel with JSON input and redacted diff rendering.

### Validation

- Ran focused desktop API/static tests: 22 tests passed.
- Ran full desktop test suite: 180 tests passed.
- Ran JavaScript syntax check with user-installed Node.js: passed.
- Ran `cargo check` for the Tauri shell: passed.
- Ran V5 release builder dry-run: passed; no files copied.
- Ran Tauri launch/close smoke: passed; backend cleanup verified.

### Regression Risk

Low. This is non-mutating and does not save PSD1 files. The main risk is operator confusion because the panel accepts raw JSON; it is intentionally labeled as preview-only until structured settings editors and a true backend patch-save contract are implemented.

## 2026-05-07 - Local API Settings Reload From Disk

### Root Problem

The local API backend resolved config paths and config values once at startup. That was acceptable for read-only prototype work, but it becomes stale as soon as the PSD1 changes on disk, and it is a blocker for any future safe settings-save endpoint. The backend needs an explicit way to refresh its resolved state without restarting the shell.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\local_api_main.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\server.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\contract.py`

- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added `BackendResolvedState` to own the local API's current `ResolvedPaths` behind a lock.
- Added token-protected `POST /api/settings/reload` with `effect=none`.
- The reload command re-runs the existing path/config resolution, updates the backend's resolved-state cache, and returns a command-result envelope with key count and path metadata.
- Added a Settings page `Reload From Disk` button that calls the backend reload command and refreshes the web snapshot.
- Kept the operation non-mutating: it does not write config, touch media, or start pipeline work.

## 2026-05-07 - Web Prototype Guarded Selected Rename Apply

### Root Problem

The web Rename page could preview selected-row final names and force-policy overrides, but it still had no way to execute the existing standalone rename transaction. Exposing a generic apply endpoint or accepting frontend-supplied plan rows would be unsafe because a browser-side stale plan could rename more files than intended or bypass backend collision checks.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\application\facade.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\contract.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\server.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\index.html`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\assets\app.js`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_application_facade.py`
- `Docs\archive\historical-reviews\TAURI_WEBVIEW2_TRANSITION_GROUNDWORK.md`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added token-protected `POST /api/rename/apply` with `effect=filesystem-mutation`.
- The endpoint requires `confirm_apply=true`.
- The endpoint requires explicit `selected_sources` and applies only rows whose source paths are selected.
- The backend rebuilds the rename plan from the current request and existing rename planner; it does not accept prebuilt row objects from the browser.
- Blocked rows are rejected before mutation.
- The actual filesystem operation uses the existing `apply_rename_path_plan()` transaction, undo manifest, collision checks, sidecar moves, metadata updates, and rollback path.
- Added a web `Apply Selected Rename` button with browser confirmation.
- After success, the web prototype replaces applied source paths in the path textarea with returned destination paths and refreshes preview.
- Deliberately did not expose Apply All in this pass.

### Validation

- Ran focused desktop API/static tests: 26 tests passed.
- Ran JavaScript syntax check with user-installed Node.js: passed.
- Ran full desktop test suite: 184 tests passed.
- Ran `cargo check` for the Tauri shell: passed.

- Ran Tauri launch/close smoke: passed; backend cleanup verified.
- Restarted the V5 local API on port 8765 and verified `/api/health` returned `ok` with exactly one `local_api_main` process.

### Regression Risk

Medium. This is the first web prototype command in this migration that can rename media files and sidecars. Risk is constrained by token auth, browser confirmation, backend plan rebuild, selected-source filtering, blocked-row rejection, and the existing transactional rename/rollback service. Apply All remains intentionally unavailable in the web prototype.

## 2026-05-07 - Web Prototype Guarded Settings Patch Save

### Root Problem

The web Settings page had read-only config rendering, validation, reload, and non-mutating patch preview, but no way to persist a controlled settings change. A full table save would be unsafe because the UI displays redacted sensitive values and could overwrite secrets. The next safe step is a backend-owned explicit patch save, not a frontend-owned config document writer.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\application\facade.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\contract.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\api\server.py`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\index.html`
- `DesktopApp\mediapipeline_desktop_app\ui_web\static\assets\app.js`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_application_facade.py`
- `Docs\archive\historical-reviews\TAURI_WEBVIEW2_TRANSITION_GROUNDWORK.md`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added token-protected `POST /api/settings/save-patch` with `effect=config-write`.
- The endpoint accepts explicit `changes`, optional `remove_keys`, and requires `confirm_save=true`.
- The backend merges changes with the unredacted resolved config, preserving sensitive values not included in the patch.
- Sensitive keys reject the literal `<redacted>` placeholder.
- Validation runs before save.
- Save uses the existing `serialize_psd1_document()` and `save_config_document()` path, including backup creation, PowerShell syntax validation, and atomic write behavior.
- After a successful save, the local API reloads resolved paths/config data so the web shell no longer serves stale settings.
- Added a guarded `Save Patch` button to the web Settings patch panel with browser confirmation and command-result logging.

### Validation

- Ran focused desktop API/static tests: 27 tests passed.
- Ran JavaScript syntax check with user-installed Node.js: passed.
- Ran full desktop test suite: 185 tests passed.
- Ran `cargo check` for the Tauri shell: passed.
- Ran V5 release builder dry-run: passed; no files copied.
- Ran Tauri launch/close smoke: passed; backend cleanup verified.
- Restarted the V5 local API on port 8765 and verified `/api/health` returned `ok` with exactly one `local_api_main` process.

### Regression Risk

Medium-high. This route can write the active PSD1 config. Risk is constrained by token auth, explicit browser/backend confirmation, backend merge with unredacted config, rejection of redacted placeholders for sensitive keys, existing config validation, backup creation, atomic write, and immediate backend reload. The UI still exposes a raw JSON patch editor; a structured settings editor should replace this before the web shell becomes the default app.

## 2026-05-09 - Rename Apply Serialization

### Root Problem

Rename apply is a filesystem mutation command. The WebView rejected apply while a preview was active, but it did not track an apply request already in flight. The backend also rebuilt and applied rename plans without a facade-level lock, so multiple Local API clients could attempt overlapping apply operations against the same files.

- `Docs\V5_TAURI_TRANSITION_CURRENT_PLAN.md`

### Implementation

- Added a facade-owned nonblocking rename-apply lock.
- Held the lock from backend plan rebuild through selected-row apply so overlapping Local API apply calls cannot race the filesystem.
- Added a standard warning result for blocked backend rename apply attempts.
- Added WebView apply-in-flight state and shared button synchronization with preview-in-flight state.
- Kept preview behavior, selected-only apply behavior, rename transaction logic, sidecar handling, and Tk behavior unchanged.

- Ran `python -m unittest discover -s DesktopApp\tests -q`: 780 tests passed.

### Regression Risk

Low-medium. This intentionally serializes rename apply operations. A legitimate second apply must wait for the first to complete, which is safer than overlapping filesystem rename transactions.

## 2026-05-09 - ActiveJobs PID-Reuse Close-Readiness Hardening

ActiveJobs close-readiness used PID liveness alone. If Windows reused the old PID from a stale pipeline launch record for an unrelated process, the future Tauri shell could keep warning about active MediaPipeline work even though the recorded PowerShell process was gone.

- Kept the existing `active_job_pid_is_alive()` helper unchanged for compatibility.
- Treated a PID as stale when the process is alive but both inspected launch identity signals clearly mismatch the ActiveJobs record.
- Continued to fail closed when process identity cannot be inspected due to access denial or other psutil failures.

- Expanded the Tauri close-readiness source test to verify the close warning includes backend reason/state details.

### Regression Risk

Low-medium. This only changes how stale ActiveJobs records are interpreted when process identity can be inspected. If identity cannot be inspected, close-readiness remains conservative and blocks close as before.

## 2026-05-14 - WebView Browser Smoke Runner Stability Sweep

### Root Problem

The browser-backed WebView smokes shared CDP setup, but each smoke still owned its own `subprocess.run` result parsing and Chrome/Edge process cleanup. The generated Node runners also launched the browser with stdout/stderr pipes that were never drained, and then waited on an `exit` event after `kill()` even if the browser had already exited. That could make an otherwise useful smoke fail as a timeout or hang instead of reporting the actual WebView/CDP assertion.

### Files Changed

- `DesktopApp\tests\webview_browser_smoke_support.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_completed_pending_proof_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_diagnostics_handoff_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_high_risk_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_large_table_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_lifecycle_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_network_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_pending_drain_guard_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_rename_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_schedule_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_settings_launch_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_webview_browser_telemetry_smoke.py`
- `DesktopApp\tests\test_tauri_shell_scaffold.py`
- `Docs\WEBVIEW_SMOKE_TEST_CATALOG.md`
- `Docs\BROWSER_SMOKE_TEST_RUNBOOK.md`
- `Docs\TLDR.md`
- `Docs\V5_TRANSITION_STATUS_BOARD.md`
- `Docs\VALIDATION_LADDER_RUNBOOK.md`
- `Docs\V5_TAURI_TRANSITION_CURRENT_PLAN.md`
- `Docs\REMEDIATION_CHANGELOG.md`

### Implementation

- Added `run_node_browser_smoke` as the shared Python execution wrapper for browser-backed Node/CDP smoke runners.
- The wrapper converts timeout failures into the same bounded failure-reporting format as normal nonzero exits, validates a JSON object result line, and reports malformed/no-output runners with bounded stdout/stderr context.
- Added shared Node/CDP `launchBrowser` and `terminateBrowser` helpers.
- Chrome/Edge is now launched with browser stdout/stderr ignored instead of undrained pipes.
- Browser cleanup now handles already-exited browser processes and uses bounded wait/kill behavior rather than waiting forever on an exit event that may already have fired.
- Updated all browser-backed smoke modules to use the shared runner and browser lifecycle helpers.
- Added static scaffold coverage that prevents regression to per-smoke `subprocess.run`, undrained browser pipes, direct browser spawn, and unbounded `browser.once("exit")` waits.

Low. This changes test/smoke infrastructure only. It does not change WebView runtime assets, backend API behavior, local API contracts, process-launch semantics, settings persistence, rename apply, pending publish, FFmpeg/media policy, Network lifecycle, Tk fallback, or V4. ### Implementation

- Added a narrow shared-runner retry for exactly the no-output native crash return codes `3221226505` and `-1073740791`.
- Added clearer CDP WebSocket open error text and extended the same single retry boundary to no-output CDP connection-open transients (`[object ErrorEvent]` / `CDP websocket error while opening`).

- Added focused unit coverage proving the shared runner retries once for the no-output native crash and CDP open transient, and does not retry a normal actionable failure.
- Hardened all browser-smoke temporary Chrome/Edge profile roots with `ignore_cleanup_errors=True` so Windows cache-file locks cannot mask the real assertion result during cleanup.
- Updated browser-smoke runbooks and triage notes to document the exact retry boundary.

## 2026-05-16 - Advanced Gate: Persistent Topbar Toggle Hides Non-Daily-Driver Panels

### Motivation

The operator dashboard has ~94 total panels across 13 pages. Only a subset is needed in a daily-driver session (health check → queue → launch → telemetry → accept completed → drain pending → rename → schedule/settings). The remaining ~59 panels — forensic evidence, advanced keys, diagnostics internals, network mode scaffolding, coverage reviews, etc. — add noise for experienced operators but remain available for auditing and troubleshooting. A persistent, low-friction toggle provides clean daily-driver mode without hiding anything permanently.

### What Changed

**`DesktopApp/mediapipeline_desktop_app/ui_web/static/assets/styles.css`**

Added an `/* ===== ADVANCED GATE ===== */` block immediately before `/* ===== REDUCED MOTION ===== */`:

```css
[data-advanced] { display: none; }
.advanced-mode [data-advanced] { display: block; }

#advanced-toggle { transition: background 150ms ease, border-color 150ms ease, color 150ms ease; }
#advanced-toggle[aria-pressed="true"] {
  background: var(--blue-700);
  color: var(--grey-50);
  border-color: var(--blue-600);
}
#advanced-toggle[aria-pressed="true"]:hover {
  background: var(--blue-600);
  border-color: var(--blue-500);
}
```

The gate is purely CSS: `[data-advanced]` elements are hidden by default; `.advanced-mode` on `<body>` reveals them. `display: block` on the wrapper div is safe — inner element layout (flex, grid, etc.) is preserved because the property applies to the wrapper, not the children.

**`DesktopApp/mediapipeline_desktop_app/ui_web/static/index.html`**

1. **Topbar button** — inserted between the close-readiness span and the existing refresh button:
   ```html
   <button type="button" id="advanced-toggle" class="secondary-button" aria-pressed="false">Advanced</button>
   ```

2. **Panel marking** — 43 `data-advanced` occurrences added across all 13 pages:

| Page | Marking strategy | Panels/groups gated |
|---|---|---|
| Home (Dashboard) | One `<div data-advanced>` wrapper around all 15 SV sub-panels (Conflict Summary through Session Handoff block) | 15 sub-panels |
| Queue | Two `<div data-advanced>` wrappers for sub-panel groups (Backend Launch Scope Preview, Backend Drain Scope Preview) | 2 groups |
| Completed (Output) | Eight `<div data-advanced>` wrappers (Run History, Output Proof, Output Verification, Evidence Packet, Route Agreement, Manifest Check, Output Checklist, Collision Risk+Excluded Files combined) | 8 groups |
| Pending (Publish) | Seven `<div data-advanced>` wrappers (size-growth sub-panels, conflict tables, coverage, final-trust, proof-review groups) | 7 groups |
| Rename | One `<div data-advanced>` wrapper (Outcome Review sub-panel) | 1 group |
| Launch | Seven `<div data-advanced>` wrappers (scope-reconciliation, pilot evidence, real-media proof, start-decision-summary sub-panel groups) | 7 groups |
| Reports | `data-advanced` attribute on full `<section class="panel">` (Pre-Launch Context section) | 1 section |
| Network (Workers) | `data-advanced` attribute on 4 full `<section class="panel">` elements (coordinator/worker topology, lifecycle, lifecycle-history) | 4 sections |
| Maintenance | No advanced panels — all content is daily-driver (toolchain health) | 0 |
| Diagnostics | `data-advanced` on 3 full sections + 5 `<div data-advanced>` wrappers (Page Handoff, Backend State, Open Files, API Contract sections; backend-detail sub-panel groups) | 8 items |
| Settings | `data-advanced` on 6 full sections (Advanced Keys, Advanced Key Plan, Safety Locks, Change Preview, Active Policy, Policy Readiness) | 6 sections |
| Schedule | No advanced panels — all schedule content is daily-driver | 0 |
| Telemetry (Live) | No advanced panels — live metrics are daily-driver | 0 |

**`DesktopApp/mediapipeline_desktop_app/ui_web/static/assets/app.js`**

Added `initAdvancedToggle()` function before the `DOMContentLoaded` listener:

```javascript
function initAdvancedToggle() {
  const STORAGE_KEY = "mediapipeline-advanced-mode";
  const btn = byId("advanced-toggle");
  if (!btn) return;

  function applyAdvancedMode(on) {
    document.body.classList.toggle("advanced-mode", on);
    btn.setAttribute("aria-pressed", String(on));
    btn.dataset.state = on ? "on" : "off";
    try { localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, on ? "1" : "0"); } catch (_) {}
  }

  let stored = false;
  try { stored = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY) === "1"; } catch (_) {}
  applyAdvancedMode(stored);

  btn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    applyAdvancedMode(!document.body.classList.contains("advanced-mode"));
  });
}
```

Called `initAdvancedToggle()` inside `DOMContentLoaded` immediately after `initNavigation()`.

### Files Modified

| File | Change type |
|---|---|
| `styles.css` | CSS rule addition (`[data-advanced]`, `.advanced-mode [data-advanced]`, `#advanced-toggle` styling) |
| `index.html` | Topbar button insertion + 43 `data-advanced` attribute/wrapper additions across 13 pages |
| `app.js` | `initAdvancedToggle()` function + call site in `DOMContentLoaded` |
| `Docs/WEBVIEW_DOM_ID_INVENTORY.md` | `advanced-toggle` row added to topbar section |

### Validation

- Full test suite: **1183 passed, 96 subtests passed**, 0 failed — `data-advanced` wrappers and section attributes are invisible to existing assertions.
- No existing `assertIn` call targets `data-advanced` text content, so no assertion drift from the gate.

### Regression Risk

Low. The gate is additive:
- CSS `[data-advanced] { display: none; }` only fires on elements with that attribute; all existing elements without it are unaffected.
- The topbar button is a new element — no existing ID collides with `advanced-toggle`.
- `initAdvancedToggle()` reads from `localStorage` on load; if the key is absent (first load), `stored` is `false` and advanced mode is off — correct default.
- Existing tests do not assert on `localStorage` state, `aria-pressed`, or `body` class names.
- Test suite result unchanged: 1183 passed, 0 failed.

## 2026-05-16 - V5 UI Stage 11: Missed Primary Button, Empty State Icon + Copy, Light Mode CSS

Closed the four deferred items from Stages 2–7 that were not covered by prior stages, plus one missed button identified during the Stage 11 audit. ### Task 0 — Missed Primary Button: Save Schedule

`schedule-editor-save-button` was incorrectly classed `danger-button`. Saving a schedule is a positive, reversible write — not destructive. Changed to `primary-button`.

- `index.html` `schedule-editor-save-button`: `class="danger-button"` → `class="primary-button"`
- Total `class="primary-button"` count: 3 → 4

Buttons intentionally left as `danger-button`: `pending-drain-button` (irreversible file move), `audit-start-button` (irreversible pipeline start), `rerun-start-button` (irreversible pipeline start), `backend-shutdown-button` (process termination).

### Task 1 — Empty State Icon (CSS `::before`)

Added a `::before` pseudo-element to `.empty-state` to provide a visual anchor above the label text. A pseudo-element avoids any DOM change.

```css
.empty-state::before {
  content: "—";
  display: block;
  font-size: var(--text-xl);
  font-weight: 300;
  color: var(--grey-600);
  margin-bottom: var(--space-3);
  letter-spacing: 0.08em;
}
```

An em-dash at `text-xl` (24 px) reads as a visual separator rather than domain-specific content. Neutral enough for all table types (errors, files, jobs, events).

### Task 2 — Empty State Copy (Context-Specific)

Replaced the generic `"No items"` / `"Items will appear here when available."` copy on all 97 empty-state instances with context-appropriate wording. Instances fall into four categories:

| Category | Label | Hint |
|---|---|---|
| A — Backend-populated (refresh to load) | `No data loaded` | `Refresh to load data from the backend.` |
| B — Selection-driven (select a row) | `No row selected` | `Select a row above to see details here.` |
| C — Live-signal (empty = healthy) | Specific per-table (see below) | Specific per-table (see below) |
| D — Scope-preview (action required) | `No preview loaded` | Specific per-table (see below) |

Category C specific wording:

| Table | Label | Hint |
|---|---|---|
| Errors (Diagnostics) | `No errors recorded` | `Errors appear here when the backend reports a failure.` |
| Events (Diagnostics) | `No events recorded` | `Events appear here when the backend emits state changes.` |
| Flagged Items (Queue) | `Nothing flagged` | `Flagged rows appear here when the backend marks a file blocked.` |
| Flagged Items (Completed) | `Nothing flagged` | `Flagged rows appear here when output validation finds a problem.` |
| Flagged Items (Pending Publish) | `Nothing flagged` | `Flagged rows appear here when the drain guard blocks a publish.` |
| Collision Risk (Queue) | `No collisions detected` | `Collision rows appear here when two queue items would write the same output path.` |
| Excluded Files (Queue) | `No exclusions` | `Excluded rows appear here when files are filtered out of the active scope.` |
| Warnings (Reports) | `No warnings` | `Warnings appear here when the backend emits advisory-level signals.` |

**Block 1 — `:root` overrides:**

```css
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) {
  :root {
    color-scheme: light;
    --grey-900: hsl(220, 4%,  95%);   /* near-white surface */
    --grey-800: hsl(220, 5%,  90%);
    --grey-700: hsl(220, 6%,  82%);
    --grey-600: hsl(220, 7%,  70%);
    --grey-500: hsl(220, 8%,  55%);
    --grey-400: hsl(220, 9%,  42%);
    --grey-300: hsl(220, 10%, 30%);
    --grey-200: hsl(220, 11%, 20%);
    --grey-100: hsl(220, 13%, 12%);
    --grey-50:  hsl(220, 15%, 7%);    /* near-black text */
    --evidence-bg: var(--purple-100);
    --shadow-1: 0 1px 2px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.08);
    --shadow-2: 0 2px 4px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.10);
    --shadow-3: 0 4px 8px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.12), 0 1px 3px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.07);
    --shadow-4: 0 8px 24px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.14), 0 2px 6px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.09);
    --shadow-5: 0 16px 48px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.16), 0 4px 12px hsl(220 15% 10% / 0.10);
    --focus-ring:       0 0 0 2px hsl(215, 55%, 56%, 0.35);
    --focus-ring-error: 0 0 0 2px hsl(5,   68%, 48%, 0.35);
  }
}
```

Grey scale is inverted — dark-mode `--grey-900` (near-black) becomes light-mode `--grey-900` (near-white). All surface, text, and border tokens resolve correctly through the inversion without touching any class names. Mid-range status colours (blue, green, amber, red, purple) require no adjustment.

**Block 2 — `::selection` override:**

```css
@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) {
  ::selection {
    background: var(--blue-500);
    color: var(--grey-900);
  }
}
```

In dark mode, `::selection` uses `--blue-700` background and `--grey-50` text (near-black). In light mode, `--grey-50` becomes near-black, which has poor contrast against medium-dark blue. The override uses `--blue-500` (medium-bright blue) and `--grey-900` (near-white) — passes WCAG AA.

## 2026-05-16 - V5 UI Stage 12: Daily-Driver Dashboard Rebuild + Kill Backend

### Summary

Complete redesign of the WebView home page from an information-dense multi-panel layout into a minimalist daily-driver dashboard. Adds a hard-kill backend action. The advanced-mode gate (from Stage 11 Advanced Gate) wraps all existing home panels so nothing is lost — operators toggle into advanced mode when they need the detail.

### Tasks

#### Task 0 — Backend: Add Hard Kill Action

**Task 0A — `facade_process_control_policy.py`:**

Added `"kill"` to `PIPELINE_CONTROL_ACTIONS` and updated the error message:

```python
# Before:
PIPELINE_CONTROL_ACTIONS = frozenset({"pause", "stop", "rescan"})
PIPELINE_CONTROL_ACTION_ERROR = "Action must be pause, stop, or rescan."

# After:
PIPELINE_CONTROL_ACTIONS = frozenset({"pause", "stop", "rescan", "kill"})
PIPELINE_CONTROL_ACTION_ERROR = "Action must be pause, stop, rescan, or kill."
```

**Task 0B — `facade_process_control.py`:**

Added `elif normalized == "kill":` branch after the `elif normalized == "rescan":` block. Uses `kill_related_pipeline_processes(resolved)` (psutil name-matching; no process handle required):

```python
elif normalized == "kill":
    method = getattr(self.service, "kill_related_pipeline_processes", None)
    if not callable(method):
        raise RuntimeError("Kill control service is not available.")
    messages = method(resolved)
    message = (
        "; ".join(messages)
        if messages
        else "No active pipeline processes found to kill."
    )
    flag_path = None
```

## 2026-05-17 - V5 UI Stage 15: Light Mode Toggle + Colour System

### Summary

Implemented a full light/dark mode system controlled by a persistent topbar toggle. Replaced the `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` approach with a JS-driven `body.light-mode` class so the operator can override the OS preference. Grey scale tokens are inverted in `body.light-mode`; status palette tokens are supplemented by per-component overrides that flip dark status backgrounds (visible only on dark surfaces) to light equivalents. Canvas chart backgrounds are theme-aware. Evidence panel accent colour switches purple → blue in light mode.

### Tasks

#### Task 1 — HTML: Theme toggle button

Added `<button type="button" id="theme-toggle" class="secondary-button">Light</button>` to `.topbar-actions`, between `#advanced-toggle` and `#refresh-button`.

#### Task 2 — app.js: `initThemeToggle()`

`initThemeToggle()` reads `localStorage` key `mediapipeline-theme` on load, falls back to `window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)')`, then calls `applyTheme(bool)` which toggles `body.light-mode` and updates button label. Click handler inverts current state. Called in `DOMContentLoaded` before `initSettingsTabNav()`.

#### Task 3 — styles.css: Light mode token overrides

Replaced `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` trigger with `body.light-mode {}` for both the grey-scale token block and `::selection`. Added 9 component fix categories (A–I):

| Category | Fix |
|---|---|
| A | Active nav button: `--blue-100` bg / `--blue-500` border |
| B | Danger button: `--red-100` bg / `--red-700` text (+ hover/active/disabled states) |
| C | Table status-row text: flip `--x-100` → `--x-700` for each status |
| D | Panel heading strong states: same flip |
| E | Selected table row: `--blue-800` → `--blue-100` bg |
| F | State pills: dark status bgs → `--x-100/--x-700` pairs |
| G | Topbar badges: same flip for ok/warning/updating/failed/safe/blocked |
| H | Home compact table dividers: `--grey-800` → `--grey-600` |
| I | Evidence panel accent: purple border → `--blue-600` |

Also changed `--evidence-bg` inside `body.light-mode {}` from `--purple-100` to `--blue-100`.

#### Task 4 — telemetryView.js: Canvas light mode

`drawTelemetryChart()` now detects `body.light-mode` class and branches chart background/grid/label colours. Dark-mode chart line colours (`#65a7ff` CPU, `#36d17d` GPU, `#ffc857` RAM) unchanged — vivid enough for both surfaces.

## 2026-05-20 - Diagnostics BridgeActions Refresh Regression

### Problem

The WebView top banner could show `Refresh failed: diagnosticsBridgeActions is not defined`. The immediate failing path was Reports diagnostics-action rendering: `reportsView.js` still called the transitional global `diagnosticsBridgeActions(...)`, but the bridge module only exposed that helper through `window.mediaPipelineDiagnosticsBridge` after later namespace cleanup. Older Launch history and command-review surfaces also still contain guarded global bridge-helper calls, so removing this specific compatibility alias was premature.

### Fix

`diagnosticsBridge.js` now restores `window.diagnosticsBridgeActions = diagnosticsBridgeActions` beside the other existing transitional diagnostics bridge aliases. The primary namespace object remains `window.mediaPipelineDiagnosticsBridge`, and new code should still prefer namespace-first access. `test_application_facade_web_static.py` now derives the diagnostics bridge helper names still consumed as legacy flat helpers and verifies each one has a matching `window.*` export, so future flat-export cleanup cannot reintroduce the refresh failure without first migrating the consumers. `WEBVIEW_GLOBAL_EXPORT_INVENTORY.md` was updated from 756 to 757 flat exports and the generated manifest now lists `diagnosticsBridgeActions`.

### Safety Boundary

This is a WebView compatibility/export fix only. It does not add or change Local API routes, diagnostics open/tail allowlists, command contracts, backend state reads, media policy, launch scope, queue planning, settings save, rename apply, pending publish drain, source/scratch/output file handling, Tauri lifecycle, or V4/Tk fallback behavior.
