## 2026-05-20 - Layout Manager Edge Cases

### Problem

Two deferred WebView layout-manager edge cases remained open after the earlier customization work. A stored custom page order could keep placing newly added panels after every existing stored panel when the authored page schema changed, making new evidence panels easy to miss. Also, dragging an advanced-gated panel gave no immediate explanation that the panel was still gated and would not behave like an always-visible customized panel until Advanced was explicitly enabled.

### Fix

`app.js` now compares the stored panel order against the current direct-child panel-key set before applying a saved order. If the page schema changed, it preserves per-panel hidden/advanced state, resets the stored order to the authored default order, marks `data-layout-order-status="schema-reset"`, and leaves newly added panels in their authored position. Drag-start on an advanced-gated panel now shows a transient local hint in the customize bar: `Still gated. Click Advanced to make this panel always visible.` The hint styling lives in `styles.layout-manager.css`.

### Safety Boundary

This is WebView local layout-state behavior only. It does not add or change Local API routes, backend command contracts, media policy, launch scope, queue planning, settings save, rename apply, pending publish drain, source/scratch/output file handling, Tauri lifecycle, or V4/Tk fallback behavior.

## 2026-05-18 - WebView Workflow Table Scanability Pass

### Problem

The Queue, Output, and Pending Publish primary workflow tables were still visually close to equal-weight data grids. Refactoring UI notes from the current UI materials call for clearer hierarchy, tighter scan paths, and status treatment that makes important states legible without increasing command prominence or moving backend-owned media policy into the WebView.

### Changes

- Added shared `workflow-table` plus page-specific `queue-table`, `completed-table`, and `pending-table` classes to the primary Queue, Output, and Publish tables.
- Added content-weighted CSS column sizing for those workflow tables using existing V5 design tokens for spacing, type, and colors.
- Added shared `makeStatusChip()` / `setCellStatusChip()` DOM helpers and inventoried the new flat `window.*` exports.

## 2026-05-18 - Backend Shutdown Fail-Closed Contract

### Problem

The local API accepted a tokened `POST /api/backend/shutdown` and scheduled backend shutdown even when `GET /api/backend/close-readiness` reported active work, an armed schedule-stop watcher, or an unreadable readiness state.

### Changes

- Changed normal unsafe backend shutdown requests to return `ok=false`, `severity="error"`, and `refresh_hint="close-readiness"` without scheduling the backend shutdown callback.
- Preserved the explicit `force_active_work_shutdown=true` path for backend-owned cleanup before shutdown.
- Updated lifecycle, command-payload, command-history, Tauri scaffold, route inventory, ownership, and smoke-wrapper assertions to expect watcher-blocked shutdown as a failure result.

## 2026-05-18 - Unknown Destination Space Fails Closed Before Copy

### Problem

`Copy-FileRobocopy` already blocked known low destination space, but a failed or timed-out free-space probe returned `-1` and still proceeded into robocopy. That meant a disconnected or unreadable destination could reach mutation/copy attempts instead of failing closed at preflight.

### Changes

- Added `OUTPUT_DESTINATION_SPACE_UNKNOWN` as a structured `Copy-FileRobocopy` preflight reason.
- Blocked destination copies before robocopy is invoked when destination free space cannot be determined.
- Kept `DestinationFreeGB=-1`, required GB estimate, and an operator-readable reason in `LastCopyFileRobocopyResult`.
- Treated unknown output destination space like output-space deferred publish when the verified local output can be safely parked in `PendingServerPush`.
- Added reliability regression coverage for both direct copy preflight and publish-completion parking behavior.

### Validation

- PowerShell parser checks passed for `Pipeline/Modules/Disk.ps1`, `Pipeline/Modules/PublishCompletion.ps1`, and `Pipeline/Tests/Invoke-ReliabilityRegressionChecks.ps1`.

## 2026-05-18 - WebView Frontend Mutation Boundary Static Gate

### Problem

The Network page had a focused read-only boundary test, and browser smokes blocked or hashed mutation paths in selected scenarios, but there was no single static test over all WebView `apiPost` call sites. A future frontend edit could add an undocumented command route, move a command call to the wrong page module, pass raw path keys to shell-open routes, bypass explicit confirmation payloads, or introduce direct filesystem/process/Tauri APIs before browser smokes noticed.

### Changes

- Added `DesktopApp/tests/test_webview_frontend_mutation_boundary.py`.
- The test verifies every WebView `apiPost(...)` call uses a literal documented POST route from `LOCAL_API_ROUTE_CONTRACT`.
- It pins current command-route ownership by JS asset so mutation-capable routes stay on their owning pages.
- It verifies shell-open routes send backend selector payloads (`row_key`/`row_scope`/`target`) and not raw path keys such as `path`, `source_path`, `destination_folder`, or `manifest`.
- It verifies `rename.apply`, `settings.save-patch`, and `schedule.save` retain explicit confirmation payloads.
- It verifies `fetch(...)` remains centralized in `apiClient.js` and rejects direct frontend filesystem/process/Tauri shell APIs.
- Updated coverage docs, the active checklist, and this touch-log/changelog record. No runtime WebView behavior, backend route contract, Local API handler, pipeline logic, config, queue state, pending publish state, or media file changed.
